To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T cell clusters formed by OKT3 are dependent on LFA‐1 and that the clusters formed by CVI patients are larger and appear at an earlier time than those formed by normal individuals.
(1) The formation of T cell‐T cell clusters is a normal phenomenon in vitro, and is triggered by the binding of OKT3 antibody to the TCR/ CD3 complex.

(i) the formation of T‐cell clusters in response to anti‐CD3 stimulation is accelerated in patients with common variable immune deficiency (CVI), and (ii) the acceleration of T‐cell clustering is due to an increase in the number of T cells carrying the activated conformation of LFA‐l.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction between T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes in the process of antibody formation.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the immunodeficiency in patients with common variable hypogammaglobulinaemia.
a better understanding of the role of adhesion molecules and the T cell receptor in the activation of T cells and in T‐cell‐B cell interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T cell clusters are formed by a LFA‐I‐dependent process, but the mechanism of this dependence is complex and requires further study.
the CVI T cells have a higher proportion of LFA‐l molecules in the activated state.
the T cell cluster formation is an important phenomenon in the pathogenesis of common variable immunodeficiencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in CVI the LFA‐1 integrin is in an activated state and that the T cell clusters are a reflection of this.

the TCR/OKT3‐drug T cell clustering in CVI patients is LFA‐1 dependent, and that the accelerated clustering and the larger clusters are due to an increase in activated LFA‐1 molecules on CVI patient's cells.

the formation of large numbers, of homotypic T cell clusters might reduce the interaction between T and B cells, thus contributing lo the depression of immunoglobin synthesis observed in this condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of T‐cell aggregates is a very sensitive assay of T‐cell activation, and that this assay may be of diagnostic value.
the T cell clusters in patients with common variable immune deficiency (CVI) were larger than normal and appeared earlier in culture.
we have identified a new mechanism of T cell activation that is dependent on LFA‐1/ICAM‐I interaction.
